en: "Venerable Nāgasena, what is the characteristic of concentration?

"Concentration, Great King, has the characteristic of being pre-eminent. Whatever wholesome states there may be, they all have concentration as their head; they incline toward concentration, lean toward concentration, and tend toward concentration."
“Just as, Great King, whatever rafters there are in a gabled house, they all go toward the peak, lean toward the peak, converge at the peak, and the peak is declared to be their chief;
even so, Great King, whatever wholesome states there are, they all have concentration as their head, lean toward concentration, incline toward concentration, and tend toward concentration.”
“Suppose, great king, some king were to enter into battle with a fourfold army;
the entire army—elephants, horses, chariots, and infantry—would have him at its head, would lean toward him, would incline toward him, and would tend toward him.”
They would all follow along that very same path.

In the same way, Great King, whatever wholesome states there may be, they all have concentration as their head, they lean toward concentration, they incline toward concentration, and they slope toward concentration.
Thus, Great King, concentration has the characteristic of being preeminent.
“Great King, this was also said by the Blessed One:
‘Monks, develop concentration; for a monk who is concentrated, monks, understands things as they truly are.
